[[Image:Barrow inequality.svg|thumb|right|300px]]

In [[geometry]], '''Barrow's inequality''' is an [[Inequality (mathematics)|inequality]] relating the [[Euclidean distance|distances]] between an arbitrary point within a [[triangle]], the vertices of the triangle, and certain points on the sides of the triangle. It is named after [[David Francis Barrow]].

==Statement==
Let ''P'' be an arbitrary point inside the [[triangle]] ''ABC''. From ''P'' and ''ABC'', define ''U'', ''V'', and ''W'' as the points where the [[angle bisector]]s of ''BPC'', ''CPA'', and ''APB'' intersect the sides ''BC'', ''CA'', ''AB'', respectively. Then Barrow's inequality states that<ref name="emb"/>

: <math>PA+PB+PC\geq 2(PU+PV+PW),\,</math>

with equality holding only in the case of an [[equilateral triangle]] and ''P'' is the center of the triangle.<ref name="emb" />

== Generalisation ==
Barrow's inequality can be extended to convex polygons. For a convex polygon with vertices <math>A_1,A_2,\ldots ,A_n </math> let <math>P</math> be an inner point and  <math>Q_1, Q_2,\ldots ,Q_n</math> the intersections of the angle bisectors of <math>\angle A_1PA_2,\ldots,\angle A_{n-1}PA_n,\angle A_nPA_1 </math> with the associated polygon sides <math>A_1A_2,\ldots ,A_{n-1}A_n, A_nA_1</math>, then the following inequality holds:<ref>M. Dinca: [https://ssmr.ro/gazeta/gmb/2009/4/articol.pdf "A Simple Proof of the Erdös-Mordell Inequality"]. In: ''Articole si Note Matematice'', 2009</ref><ref>Hans-Christof Lenhard: "Verallgemeinerung und Verschärfung der Erdös-Mordellschen Ungleichung für Polygone". In: ''Archiv für Mathematische Logik und Grundlagenforschung'', Band 12, S. 311–314, [[doi:10.1007/BF01650566]] (German).</ref>

:<math>\sum_{k=1}^n|PA_k|\geq \sec\left(\frac{\pi}{n}\right) \sum_{k=1}^n|PQ_k|</math>

Here <math>\sec(x)</math> denotes the [[Trigonometric_functions#Right-angled_triangle_definitions|secant function]]. For the triangle case <math>n=3</math> the inequality becomes Barrow's inequality due to <math>\sec\left(\tfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=2</math>.

==History==
[[File:Ungleichung barrow2.svg|thumb|upright=1.25|Barrow strengthening Erdős-Mordell<br/><math>\begin{align}&\quad\, |PA|+|PB|+|PC| \\ &\ge 2 (|PQ_a|+|PQ_b|+|PQ_c|)\\  &\ge 2 (|PF_a|+|PF_b|+|PF_c|)\end{align}</math>]]
Barrow's inequality strengthens the [[Erdős–Mordell inequality]], which has identical form except with ''PU'', ''PV'', and ''PW'' replaced by the three distances of ''P'' from the triangle's sides. It is named after [[David Francis Barrow]]. Barrow's proof of this inequality was published in 1937, as his solution to a problem posed in the [[American Mathematical Monthly]] of proving the Erdős–Mordell inequality.<ref name="emb">{{citation
 | last1 = Erdős | first1 = Paul | author1-link = Paul Erdős
 | last2 = Mordell | first2 = L. J. | author2-link = Louis J. Mordell
 | last3 = Barrow | first3 = David F. | author3-link = David Francis Barrow
 | issue = 4
 | journal = [[American Mathematical Monthly]]
 | jstor = 2300713
 | pages = 252–254
 | title = Solution to problem 3740
 | volume = 44
 | year = 1937 | doi=10.2307/2300713}}.</ref> This result was named "Barrow's inequality" as early as 1961.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Oppenheim | first = A. | authorlink = Alexander Oppenheim
 | doi = 10.1007/BF02417793
 | journal = [[Annali di Matematica Pura ed Applicata]]
 | mr = 124774
 | pages = 157–163
 | title = New inequalities for a triangle and an internal point
 | volume = 53
 | year = 1961}}</ref>

A simpler proof was later given by [[Louis J. Mordell]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Mordell | first = L. J. | author-link = Louis J. Mordell
 | issue = 357
 | journal = [[The Mathematical Gazette]]
 | jstor = 3614019
 | pages = 213–215
 | title = On geometric problems of Erdös and Oppenheim
 | volume = 46
 | year = 1962}}.</ref>
